facts.f: Greenhouse gases like carbon dioxide and methane trap heat in the air.
facts.e: More of these gases make Earth warmer. This is called global warming.

facts.f: Burning coal, oil and gas releases carbon dioxide.
facts.e: These are called fossil fuels. Using less of them helps slow climate change.

facts.f: Trees take in carbon dioxide and give out oxygen.
facts.e: They also give shade, homes for animals and help bring rain.

facts.f: Reduce, Reuse and Recycle help cut down waste.
facts.e: Reduce what you use, reuse things again and again, and recycle what you can.

facts.f: Plastic can take hundreds of years to break down.
facts.e: Carrying a cloth bag instead of a plastic bag helps.

facts.f: Biodegradable waste, like fruit peels and leaves, breaks down naturally.
facts.e: Microbes in the soil turn it back into nutrients.

facts.f: Composting turns kitchen and garden waste into rich manure.
facts.e: Worms and microbes do the work, and plants love the result.

facts.f: In India, wet waste goes in the green bin and dry waste in the blue bin.
facts.e: Separating waste at home makes recycling and composting possible. Since April 2026, sanitary waste and special-care waste (like old medicines and bulbs) must also be kept separate.

facts.f: Solar, wind and water power are renewable energy sources.
facts.e: They will not run out, unlike coal and oil.

facts.f: Fossil fuels formed from the remains of plants and animals that lived millions of years ago.
facts.e: Heat and pressure underground slowly changed them into coal, oil and gas.

facts.f: World Environment Day is celebrated on 5 June.
facts.e: The United Nations set it up in 1972, and it was first celebrated in 1973.

facts.f: Earth Day is celebrated on 22 April.
facts.e: The first Earth Day was held in 1970.

facts.f: In the Chipko Movement of the 1970s, villagers in the Himalayas hugged trees to stop them being cut.
facts.e: 'Chipko' means 'to stick' or 'to hug'. Gaura Devi and Sunderlal Bahuguna were among its leaders.

facts.f: In 1730, Amrita Devi Bishnoi and hundreds of Bishnois gave their lives to protect khejri trees in Khejarli, Rajasthan.
facts.e: The Bishnoi community is famous for protecting trees and animals.

facts.f: Project Tiger was launched in India in 1973 to protect tigers.
facts.e: It set up special tiger reserves across the country.

facts.f: Rainwater harvesting means collecting and storing rainwater for later use.
facts.e: Water from rooftops can be stored in tanks or used to refill the ground water.

facts.f: Turn off the tap while brushing your teeth.
facts.e: This simple habit can save many litres of water every day.

facts.f: Melting glaciers and ice sheets make sea levels rise.
facts.e: Warmer water also expands and takes up more space.

facts.f: The Montreal Protocol of 1987 helped protect the ozone layer.
facts.e: Countries agreed to stop using chemicals called CFCs that damage ozone. The ozone layer is slowly healing.

facts.f: In the Paris Agreement of 2015, countries agreed to try to limit global warming.
facts.e: The aim is to keep warming well below 2 °C above pre-industrial levels.

facts.f: Acid rain is caused by gases like sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides from factories and vehicles.
facts.e: Acid rain can harm forests, lakes and even old buildings like the Taj Mahal.

facts.f: Biodiversity means the variety of all living things in a place.
facts.e: Places with high biodiversity have many kinds of plants, animals and microbes.

facts.f: The Great Indian Bustard is a critically endangered bird.
facts.e: Only a small number are left, mostly in Rajasthan.

facts.f: The dodo was a flightless bird from the island of Mauritius.
facts.e: It became extinct in the 1600s, soon after people arrived.

facts.f: Cheetahs had died out in India by 1952. In 2022, cheetahs were brought to Kuno National Park.
facts.e: They were brought from Namibia and later South Africa.

facts.f: A food chain shows who eats whom.
facts.e: For example: grass is eaten by a deer, and the deer is eaten by a tiger.

facts.f: Bees pollinate many of the crops we eat.
facts.e: Without pollinators, many fruits and vegetables could not grow.

facts.f: The Ramsar Convention of 1971 protects important wetlands around the world.
facts.e: India has many Ramsar sites, like Chilika Lake and Keoladeo National Park.

facts.f: Loudness of sound is measured in decibels (dB).
facts.e: Very loud noise over a long time can damage hearing.

facts.f: LED bulbs use much less electricity than old-style filament bulbs.
facts.e: They also last much longer.

facts.f: Solar panels turn sunlight directly into electricity.
facts.e: They work even on cloudy days, though less well.

facts.f: The Air Quality Index (AQI) tells us how clean or polluted the air is.
facts.e: A higher AQI number means more polluted air.

facts.f: Tree roots hold soil together.
facts.e: When forests are cut down, rain can wash the soil away. This is called soil erosion.

facts.f: Sacred groves are patches of forest protected by local communities for religious reasons.
facts.e: They are found across India and protect many rare plants and animals.

facts.f: The 'Save Silent Valley' movement protected a rainforest in Kerala.
facts.e: It became Silent Valley National Park in 1984.

facts.f: Sea turtles sometimes mistake plastic bags for jellyfish and eat them.
facts.e: This can make them very sick. Keeping plastic out of the sea saves lives.

facts.f: A carbon footprint is the total amount of greenhouse gases caused by a person's activities.
facts.e: Walking, cycling and saving electricity make your footprint smaller.

facts.f: Walking, cycling and using buses or trains cause less pollution than going everywhere by car.
facts.e: They also keep you fit!

facts.f: Electric vehicles give out no exhaust fumes from a tailpipe.
facts.e: They help keep city air cleaner.

facts.f: Wangari Maathai of Kenya started the Green Belt Movement, which planted millions of trees.
facts.e: In 2004 she became the first African woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize.

facts.f: India's vultures nearly disappeared because of a painkiller called diclofenac given to cattle.
facts.e: Vultures that ate dead cattle were poisoned. The drug was banned for animals in 2006.

facts.f: Earthworms are called 'farmers' friends'.
facts.e: They loosen the soil and make it rich.

facts.f: World Water Day is observed on 22 March.
facts.e: It reminds us to save water and keep it clean.
